files.purpose: MCPSetupPanel.swift holds the singleton floating panel MCPSetupPanel.shared that appears when an MCP server refuses on its own side (the needsSetup state): the first presentation for a server opens the guide's pageURL in the browser, and a re-entry guard keyed on the recorded entry id makes a repeated present for the same server only order the panel front, so a failing re-check never reopens the page or rebuilds the steps. It also defines MCPSetupPanelView, the SwiftUI content: header (MCPIcon 26, entry name, guide title, xmark close), the guide reason, numbered step rows, the guide.pageLabel button, Check again or a Checking spinner, the post-check status line (needsSetup warning or failed message), and a 'Connected · N tools' success view that closes the panel 1.2 s after the server connects. In B3 the class no longer owns its NSPanel, its Escape key monitor or its placement code: it subclasses the new FloatingGuidePanel (FloatingGuidePanel.swift) with width 400 and keeps only presentedEntryID, isPresenting, present(entry:guide:model:), a close() override and fit(height:).

feature_notes: B2->B3 (commit d70cff8fe 'refactor: audit cleanups - five bug fixes, shared MCP and provider code, layer rules restored'): the NSPanel creation (makePanel, B2 :63-86), the Escape monitor (startEscapeMonitor/stopEscapeMonitor, B2 :88-100), the measure/size/place/order-front block of present (B2 :34-42) and the private panel/escapeMonitor properties (B2 :10-11) moved into the new base class FloatingGuidePanel (FloatingGuidePanel.swift, 71 lines). MCPSetupPanel now declares ': FloatingGuidePanel', calls super.init(width: 400) (:12) and present(content) (:32).

close() became 'override func close()' (:35-38): it clears presentedEntryID and calls super.close(), which stops the Escape monitor and orders the panel out. B2 stopped the monitor before clearing the id; the reorder is not observable (all synchronous on the main actor).
Escape still resets presentedEntryID: the base monitor calls self.close() (FloatingGuidePanel.swift:62), which dispatches dynamically to this override because FloatingGuidePanel is a non-final class.

Every constant is unchanged: width 400 (now the base's width), 100-pt height floor, 24-pt top-right inset, same style mask (.nonactivatingPanel, .fullSizeContentView, .titled, .closable), .floating level, [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary], hidden window buttons, key code 53. No observable behaviour changed.

MCPSetupPanelView (B2 :103-262) is byte-identical and shifted by -50 lines to B3 :53-212. Line map: B2 1-9 = B3 1-9; B2 10-11 removed; B2 12-13 = B3 10-11; B2 14 -> B3 12 (changed); B2 15-33 = B3 13-31 (-2); B2 34-42 -> B3 32; B2 43-44 = B3 33-34; B2 45-49 -> B3 35-38; B2 50-61 = B3 39-50 (-11); B2 62-100 moved to FloatingGuidePanel.swift 33-70; B2 101-262 = B3 51-212 (-50).
MCPKeyPanel.swift was refactored onto the same base in the same commit (width 380) and still has no re-entry guard, so the setup/key panel asymmetry recorded by PR-MCP-214 still holds.
unresolved_questions: Port observation, not a B3 change (ENGINEERING DECISION needed by the merge/unit owner): the C# port src/Marrow.App/Views/Settings/MCPSetupPanel.cs shows the panel with window.Show() and handles Escape through the window's own KeyDown, and has none of the ED-063 WH_CBT non-activation hook that MCPKeyPanel.cs has. PR-MCP-215 (non-activating, ordered front without activating) and PR-MCP-216 (application-wide Escape monitor) are marked IMPLEMENTED, so either the status is wrong for the setup panel or the behaviour lives somewhere not found by grep. Sharing a C# FloatingGuidePanel base, as B3 now does, would resolve this.
